source_title: Centre joins probe into Kuno cheetah cub’s death; the last one was shot in India 79 years ago - The Times of India
source_excerpt: Bhopal: The Union govt has deputed a high-level team to probe the alleged shooting, viewing it with âutmost gravityâ. It will work with the joint forest-police Special Task Force (STF) formed on October 27, which has seven days to report. Officials said several suspects have been questioned, and some nomadic hunters living nearby have reportedly left the area.The central team comprises the Inspector General of Forests of National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), the additional director of Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) and a WCCB regional deputy director. It will examine the circumstances and evidence and coordinate with the state forest department for âstrict and swift actionâ. It will also review the security, monitoring and protection measures around Kuno, and report to Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, which will then issue directions to the state govt and field authorities.The four-member STF, formed under an order signed by principal secretary (forest) Raghwendra Kumar Singh after the CT scan and surgery found pellets, has these members: the officer in charge, State Tiger Strike Force, Madhya Pradesh, Bhopal (as chairman); and two members, DSP, STF Police Unit, Gwalior; and deputy forest officer, Kuno Wildlife Forest Division, Vijaypur and one member secretary, i.e. deputy forest officer, Sheopur Regional Forest Division, Vijaypur. Its report is due to the state govt by around November 3.The cheetah cub, KNG22, a 19-month-old male and one of Nirvaâs offspring, was allegedly shot on the night of October 24. Trackers spotted it at the same location on the morning of October 25 and again around noon, but the animal had not moved. Concerned by its condition, forest officials decided to rescue it and arrange medical treatment. The cub was brought to Jabalpur at 11.50 pm on October 26, but succumbed to its injuries at 5.10 am on October 27. The cub belonged to the cheetah population brought back to India under its flagship Project Cheetah.Insiders say a couple has been rounded up for questioning on the basis of initial information. Officials have not named them or said what role, if any, they are suspected of playing. No arrest has been announced.The more significant lead concerns the people who are no longer there. Officials found that a group of traditional poachers, who had been put up in the huts of another nomadic community, probably to hunt bushmeat, fled the area soon after forest officers began their probe. Their departure, timed to the start of the inquiry, has made them a focus for investigators, who are now trying to establish who they are, how long they stayed and where they have gone.The area was on the radar of investigative agencies before the cub was found. It has been linked to the poaching of several leopards, and agencies recently seized 10 leopard skins in Agra. Officials have not said whether the two cases are connected or whether the same network is involved. Investigators are checking whether the hunters who fled had any link to that trade. Officials say one possibility being examined is that a poacher shot at the cheetah, mistaking it for a leopard, or fired during a chance encounter while hunting other wildlife. This is one line of inquiry.The last cheetah killing 79 yrs agoThe last cheetah killing in India was recorded in Dec 1947. A Maharaja had shot three cheetahs in the sal forests of Koriya, then a princely state and now a district in Chhattisgarh, which was part of undivided Madhya Pradesh. They are widely regarded as the last wild cheetahs recorded in India.The 1947 kill is documented because the hunter publicised it, say officials. A photograph of Maharaja Ramanuj Pratap Singh Deo posing with his rifle behind the dead animals was sent to Bombay Natural History Society, whose journal published it in 1948 as a rare feat. India declared the cheetah extinct in 1952. Cheetahs returned from Namibia in September 2022 under Project Cheetah, with Kuno as the main site. The present shooting is being investigated as a wildlife crime, and no one has been identified as responsible. Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey has filed a petition before the high court demanding a CBI inquiry. Chief wildlife warden Samita Rajora also reached Kuno to coordinate with the probe team.What the evidence showsVeterinarians at Nanaji Deshmukh Veterinary Science University (NDVSU), Jabalpur, provide the main evidence. They received the cub at 11:50 pm on October 26 with multiple wounds, hindlimb paralysis and urinary retention, which suggested possible spinal trauma. A CT scan found several metallic foreign bodies in and around the spine: in the body of the first lumbar vertebra (L1), between L1 and the 13th thoracic vertebra (T13), and ventral to T13. Two lay under the skin near the left shoulder. Another was within the tissue of the right lung. Under Professor and Head Dr Shobha Jawre and Professor Dr Randhir Singh, the team operated under general anaesthesia and removed five firearm pellets. The cub died at about 5:10 am on October 27. Medical examinations corroborated multiple internal injuries associated with the recovered pellets.
